Where it began

Jasprit Bumrah was born on 6 December 1993 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and played for his school side at Nirman High School. He learned his yorker by practising with a tennis ball, a habit that would cost a great many batsmen their stumps.

In 2010, at the Gujarat under-19 district trials, the selectors were unsure about his unusual action and left him out of the main squad, naming him only as a reserve. When the reserves were finally given a game, he took seven wickets. Before long he was winning a domestic final for Gujarat, and John Wright, then scouting for the Mumbai Indians, had signed him up.

The player

He first played Test cricket on 5 January 2018, at Cape Town, and the first man he dismissed was AB de Villiers. That first year he took five wickets in an innings in South Africa, England and Australia, the first Asian bowler to manage all three in one calendar year, and finished the year with 48 wickets, more than any Indian had managed in a first year of Test cricket. In 2019 he took a Test hat-trick against West Indies.

No one took more Test wickets in 2024 than his 71, and in the Border–Gavaskar series that winter he took 32, the most by an Indian bowler in any series overseas. By October 2026 he had 234 wickets from 52 Tests at an average of 19.79, with 16 five-wicket hauls and a best of six for 27. He has also led India in three Tests.

What made him special

Everything about him is a little different. The run-up is short, with small stuttering steps; the arm is straight and stiff; and the elbow bends back past where elbows usually go, so the ball leaves his hand nearer the batsman than anyone expects. He swings it both ways, reverses it, and it reaches the batsman sooner than he bargains for. Add a fine off-cutter and a yorker on demand, and batsmen rarely know what is coming.

His Test batting average is 6.57, which is about what you would expect from a man whose real work is done at the other end.

Away from the middle

He has been a Wisden Cricketer of the Year, was the ICC's Test Cricketer of the Year for 2024, picking up its Sobers Trophy as well, and taken the BCCI's Polly Umrigar Award three times. He was player of the tournament when India won the 2024 T20 World Cup, and player of the match in the 2026 final. He is married to the presenter Sanjana Ganesan.

And finally

For all that batting average, he holds a Test batting record. In 2022, captaining India against England, he took 29 runs off a single over from Stuart Broad, edging past Brian Lara's old mark of 28. Bowlers everywhere quietly enjoyed it.
